bull_bear.body: Disciplined organic investment in tech/automation and new verticals; Strong balance sheet (Rs 4,500 Cr cash) enables potential inorganic opportunities; Focus on ROIC expansion (now 16%) and sustaining free cash flow generation.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Fuel price volatility impacting consumption; Regulatory changes on gig-worker wages; Competitive intensity from marketplace 1P logistics (though management views 3P as structurally cheaper); Execution risk in scaling new verticals (cross-border/financial).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and disciplined; Emphasis on 'profitable growth' and 'capital efficiency'; Celebratory of hitting FCF positive early; Pragmatic on competition (dismisses Amazon 3PL threat as 'old news'); Forward-looking on automation to counter labor tightness.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management explicitly states that 1P logistics is structurally more expensive than 3P even after margins, suggesting a long-term structural shift of volume back to 3P as marketplaces face regulatory/labor cost pressures; The 'Delhivery Direct' app is quietly capturing significant SME/D2C share outside of aggregator channels; FCF positivity achieved despite full-year Ecom Express integration costs.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Employee stock options are a stated part of the compensation structure: as of Jun 30, 2026, ESOPs granted comprise 61,07,155 vested (unexercised) shares (0.8% of shares outstanding on a fully diluted basis) and 1,58,33,027 unvested (2.0%).
- An additional ungranted pool is disclosed — time-based ESOPs of 1,71,67,822 shares (2.1% fully diluted) and performance-based ESOPs of 1,59,00,000 shares (2.0% fully diluted).
- Performance-based ESOPs are tied to share-price milestones: to be unlocked in three equal tranches upon achieving share prices of ₹800, ₹1,000 and ₹1,200, and vest equally over 2 years thereafter; time-based ESOP vesting typically ranges from 3 to 4 years from the date of grant.
- The estimated non-cash P&L charge for ESOPs already granted is given as ₹139 Cr in FY27, ₹94 Cr in FY28, ₹42 Cr in FY29 and ₹7 Cr in FY30, with a deck-stated total of ₹283 Cr (reversible in the event of forfeiture upon resignation/termination prior to completion of vesting).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Express: Rs 1,832 Cr revenue (Q4), +46% YoY, 306 Mn volumes; PTL: Rs 622 Cr revenue (Q4), +20% YoY, 2 Mn metric tons (FY26); Transport Combined: Rs 2,453 Cr (Q4), 7.9% adj. EBITDA margin; SCS: Rs 729 Cr (FY26), margin pivoted from 2.2% to 10.9% service EBITDA.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rising fuel costs and labor wages squeezing logistics margins industry-wide | Delhivery Limited | beneficiary | High | Superior pass-through mechanisms (indexed contracts) and AI-driven cost reductions allow Delhivery to protect margins better than smaller peers; FCF inflection de-risks the equity story. |
| Marketplaces (Amazon/Flipkart) facing higher 1P logistics costs due to new gig-worker laws and minimum wage hikes | Delhivery Limited | beneficiary | Med | Structural cost disadvantage of 1P networks vs 3P will likely force marketplaces to shift more volume to third-party providers like Delhivery to optimize P&L. |
| Smaller 3PL players lacking capital for automation and tech moats face margin compression | Unorganized Logistics Players | loser | Med | Delhivery's scale and Rs 4,500 Cr cash pile allow aggressive investment in AGVs/AI that smaller players cannot match, widening the cost gap. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Reach is framed by coverage: 18,810 pin-codes served in Q1FY27, defined by the deck as unique pin-codes out of the 19,500 pin-codes as per India Post on which at least one shipment was delivered during the period (18,857 in Q1FY26; 18,830 in Q4FY26).
- 220+ countries and territories served (through Delhivery and partner networks), unchanged across Q1FY26, Q4FY26 and Q1FY27.
- Customer base described as 54,096 active customers in Q1FY27 versus 43,022 in Q1FY26 — active customers being those where an invoice was raised at least once during the quarter, excluding the count of Delhivery direct customers.
- The business is presented across five reported service lines: Transport (Express + PTL), Supply Chain Services, Others (Full truckload and Cross border), New initiatives (Delhivery Local, Rapid and Financial services), and corporate.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Ecom Express] The deck repeatedly carves out integration costs of the acquired Ecom Express business, quantified as ₹90 Cr for Q2FY26, ₹35 Cr for Q3FY26, ₹22 Cr for Q4FY26, ₹17 Cr for Q1FY27 and ₹148 Cr for FY26, described as net temporary costs pertaining to infrastructure, people, overheads, and business to be discontinued.
- [Ecom Express] Revenue from services in the service-line profitability table is stated to exclude revenue from Local, Rapid and Financial services, and Ecom Express businesses being transitioned — signalling that part of the acquired book is being wound down rather than retained.
- [Restatement basis] The quarterly income statement presents 'mgt. est.' columns for Q4FY26 and Q1FY27 that exclude the impact of Ecom Express related integration cost, so two different sets of figures for the same quarter appear in the deck (e.g. Q4FY26 revenue from services of ₹2,850 Cr reported versus ₹2,848 Cr on a management-estimate basis).
- [One-time items] Supply Chain Services FY25 adjusted EBITDA of ₹(64) Cr is attributed to a one-time impact of provisions on account of contractual matters, and Q2FY25 includes a reversal of ₹21 Cr of vendor advance provisions on account of settlement in our favour.
- [Associate] The income statement carries a separate 'share of profit / (loss) of associate (net)' line — ₹(3) Cr in Q1FY27, ₹9 Cr in Q4FY26 and ₹(8) Cr in Q1FY26 — but the deck does not name the associate.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Fuel price hikes (~Rs 3/liter) being passed through via indexed contracts (DPH clauses) and air surcharges; Q4 margins expanded despite fuel headwinds due to network productivity gains; Labor cost inflation mitigated by automation (AGVs, robotics) and AI-driven claims/documentation efficiency.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Express volume grew 72-73% YoY in Q4; Margin: Express targeting 16-18% normative range, PTL margins expanding sequentially; Order Inflow: SCS pipeline margin-accretive with strict hurdle rates; Capex: Intensity reduced to 4.7% of revenue, targeting ~4% going forward, unaffected by AI/robotics pilots.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: SCS business turned profitable with Rs 79 Cr service EBITDA (4x YoY); 2 new mandates signed/activated in Q4; Pipeline described as 'healthy' and focused on consumer durables, auto, and lifestyle sectors with disciplined client selection.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: New verticals funded by core cash flows: Local delivery, Cross-border logistics, Rapid (quick commerce enablement), and Financial services; Tech moat via Delhivery Labs deploying LLMs, AGVs, and automation to reduce unit costs and labor dependency.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Delhivery delivered a bellwether FY26 with >1B parcels shipped and a decisive pivot to free cash flow positivity (Rs 89 Cr) one year ahead of schedule, driven by record volumes in Express/PTL and a margin turnaround in Supply Chain. The core thesis shifts from growth-at-all-costs to capital-efficient scaling, with ROIC expanding to 16% and net working capital compressing to 11 days, validating the operating leverage of the integrated network.

open.item: Shift intra-city fleet from spot to long-term fixed contracts to lock in rates for next year and avoid peak-season cost spikes.
Rs. 7 crore additional oxygen-concentrator recovery expected over the next four to six quarters (Rs. 21 cr of Rs. 28 cr already recovered/reversed).
~Rs.3 diesel/pump price increase to be passed through via diesel-price-hike clauses (already showing in air-shipping Rs.1-2 increases); some near-term consumption headwind possible.
Merging the rapid and non-rapid (express) networks to improve rapid-commerce profitability, expected to start playing out by Q1 of next FY.
AGV pilots in mega gateways (Bombay) to scale up / expand to other mega gateways within this year, driven by tightening labor; not material to capex trajectory.
New-initiative (Delhivery Direct, Rapid, cross-border, financial services) investment guided at ~Rs. 130-160 crore over the next year.
New mid-size facilities in Chennai, Hyderabad (Medchal) and Noida built with a 3-4 year horizon, expected to last until fiscal 2027.
Overall adjusted EBITDA (6.3% transport in FY26) has potential to reach at least ~10%-11% of revenue (Express+PTL ~18%, corporate overheads to ~7%).
Corporate overheads expected to decline to ~7% of revenue (from ~9%) as part of the adjusted-EBITDA improvement path.
No single-customer concentration concern until a customer crosses ~35% of revenue (largest was 16% last year, now higher but well below 35%).
E-commerce industry expected to grow 15%-20% into the medium term (Delhivery a downstream beneficiary).
Capex intensity (4.7% in FY26, down from 7.8% FY23) expected to reach the ~4% target; AI and robotics investments will not materially alter the trajectory.
SCS pipeline (breakeven achieved, service EBITDA 4x to Rs.79 cr) to remain margin-accretive with every new client meeting an internal hurdle rate.
Transport ROIC (16% in FY26) targeted to reach 25%+ in steady state, driven by margin expansion and ~2-3 pts capital-intensity improvement.
PTL service EBITDA margin expected to keep expanding toward ~18% (a key driver of ROIC improvement).
Building utilization-indexed / dynamic (route-, time-, weight-, client-based) pricing to give lane discounts while improving profitability; expected to be solved over the next couple of quarters.
Delhivery will not unbundle/disintermediate its integrated network to participate in third-party platforms (e.g. Valmo).

verdicts.note: Express service EBITDA expanded to the upper end of 16-18% as retained Ecom volumes filled the network - FY26 margin expansion delivered.

verdicts.item: PTL service EBITDA margins (10.8% in Q4) expected to reach Express-like full-potential margins as freight approaches ~175,000-200,000 tons/qtr.
verdicts.note: PTL freight 549k MT/quarter (~183k/month, above the 175-200k threshold), gross margin 28% and service EBITDA 'getting closer to 18%' - near but not yet at Express-level full-potential margins. [±10% r…

verdicts.item: FY26 volume growth expected to broadly track market growth; insourcing headwind not expected to be as large as before.
verdicts.note: Q4 Express +46% revenue / +72-73% volume, far above ~15-20% market; 1P share declined - grew well above market, insourcing headwind reversed.

verdicts.item: Management expects competitors' unsustainable pricing/capital constraints to force pricing action or exit, benefiting Delhivery within a couple of quarters.
verdicts.note: 'one of them is no longer here with us' (Ecom acquired); 'I don't see a reason for them [Xpressbees] to exist'; market more settled - consolidation benefiting Delhivery.

verdicts.item: Rapid (2-hour) commerce business expected to add ~Rs. 80-100 crore of revenue through the financial year, at Express-like margins; ~50 dark stores planned in the top eight cities.
verdicts.note: Rapid commerce still a 'long cycle bet' being invested in; the Rs.80-100 cr FY26 revenue / 50-store scale-up was not achieved (build-out deferred). [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Corporate overheads (8.9% of revenue in Q3) on a glide path down toward 6% of revenues.
verdicts.note: Vivek cites corporate overheads going down to '7% of revenue' in the ROIC bridge - on the glide path but target now framed nearer 7% (still above 6%).

verdicts.item: PTL service EBITDA margin (3.8% in Q3, highest in 11 quarters) expected to keep improving, at a faster pace than Express.
verdicts.note: 'PTL margins expanded again successively'; gross margins 14% to 28% - continued improvement toward Express-level.

verdicts.item: PTL service EBITDA margins expected to rise from +3% to the +15%/+16% range as volumes grow, mirroring Express; yield improvements would be additive.
verdicts.note: PTL margins 'expanded again successively'; Vivek 'PTL getting closer to 18%'; gross margin 28% - progressing toward/through 15-16% with yield additive, not explicitly at target. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Internal ambition to grow the PTL business ~25%-30% in FY26, well above the flattish/low-single-digit industry.
verdicts.note: FY26 PTL revenue +~19% / volume +~18%; Q4 +20% - strong but below the 25-30% internal ambition (in line with the revised ~20% guidance). [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Express Parcel steady-state service EBITDA margins expected to remain in the 17%-20% range (18%-20% reiterated), potentially higher if price discounts no longer needed.
verdicts.note: Express 'firmly at the upper end' of the 16-18% range (~18%), within the 17-20% steady-state expectation.
